claims.claim: **All patients become functionally asplenic** and are at risk of infection with encapsulated organisms (pneumococcus, meningococcus, *Haemophilus*).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Crises may be spontaneous or triggered by** infection, dehydration, hypoxia, or sedatives, local anaesthetics and surgery. SS disease, sickle β-thalassaemia and HbSC disease are all treated the same way.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Many presentations need urgent treatment, and discussion with the on-call Haematology Consultant is mandatory.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Investigations:** FBE with reticulocytes · group and crossmatch · if febrile, blood and urine cultures · if jaundiced or dehydrated, U&E and LFT · consider CXR if febrile with respiratory symptoms. **Compare the spleen with the patient's baseline**; do a neurological examination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Start analgesia promptly and treat pain aggressively.** Mild: paracetamol or ibuprofen. **Moderate to severe: morphine 0.05 mg/kg/dose IV, repeated as necessary**; some benefit from PCA.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fluids:** push oral fluids; IV if needed — **bolus 10–20 mL/kg 0.9% saline** if required, then maintenance (Plasma-Lyte 148 + 5% glucose, or 0.9% sodium chloride + 5% glucose).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid excess fluids after initial resuscitation** (chest crisis risk). **Do not delay IV fluids or analgesia for topical anaesthetic cream.** Transfusion may be needed — discuss with the haematologist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat all pain initially as vaso-occlusive** — but chest pain with respiratory symptoms may be acute chest syndrome.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Life-threatening; patients may deteriorate quickly.** Lung infarction: hypoxaemia, lower respiratory symptoms and a new infiltrate on CXR — **the only signs may be hypoxaemia and chest pain. Treat chest pain as acute chest syndrome.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV 3rd-generation cephalosporin plus atypical cover (roxithromycin or azithromycin)**; the CXR must not delay treatment. **Oxygen to keep saturation over 96%** or for comfort.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Refer early to PICU** for significant hypoxia or respiratory distress.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fever: IV 3rd-generation cephalosporin** (add atypical cover if there is a significant respiratory component) and **blood and urine cultures**. Treat co-existing pain as a vaso-occlusive crisis and cough or dyspnoea as acute chest syndrome concurrently.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Definition:** Hb drop of at least 20 g/L below the patient's baseline with an acutely enlarged spleen; often mild–moderate thrombocytopenia; reticulocytes at or above baseline. **Low reticulocytes → consider co-existent aplasia.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hypovolaemia: 0.9% sodium chloride 10–20 mL/kg while blood is awaited.** Initial transfusion to aim for **Hb 5–6 g/dL** to treat shock (the page adds 'not >3 g/dL').
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not raise Hb too far or too fast** — the spleen shrinks and autotransfuses, overshooting Hb with a **risk of stroke from hyperviscosity.** IV 3rd-generation cephalosporin if febrile.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Aplastic crisis:** Hb below baseline with a markedly reduced reticulocyte count (usually under 1%), usually with acute infection including parvovirus; the spleen may also be enlarged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV plus oral fluids to a total of maintenance. Transfuse red cells if symptomatic or Hb under 5 g/dL — do not increase Hb by more than 3 g/dL.** IV 3rd-generation cephalosporin if febrile.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **About 10% of HbSS patients have an acute neurological event** — either suddenly or complicating an aplastic crisis or acute chest syndrome.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Image without delay: MRI is the modality of choice; if unavailable, CT with NO contrast** (hyperviscosity risk worsens the neurological state).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Transfusion is required:** e.g. a simple transfusion first, to **Hb 10 g/dL**, then **red cell exchange** (in ICU acutely).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Two forms:** stuttering episodes of 2–4 hrs (often recurrent, may precede a severe episode) and **severe attacks over 4 hrs, which can cause impotence.** Most common in adolescence.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Empty the bladder (catheterise if needed); moderate exercise, bath or shower. Do NOT use ice.** Start hydration, oxygen, analgesia and urinary alkalinisation as soon as possible.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Priapism beyond 4 hours: urological emergency** — involve the on-call haematologist and General Surgery (Urology).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Sickle cell disease' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Sickle_cell_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23
